linkages: cancer cases identified in the Danish cancer register and linked to the hospitalisation register to exclude earlier cancer or benign tumour diagnoses
control group drawn from the basic population registers, matched to the cancer group by base year, gender and age (10 controls per cancer case, drawn without replacement across base years)

individuals linked to job skill requirements through their Danish occupation (DISCO) code, which is linked to US SOC codes in O*NET via crosswalks (SOC 2010 to DISCO08, DISCO08 to ISCO08, ISCO88 to DISCO88, ISCO88 to ISCO08)
the DISCO88/DISCO08 crosswalk was checked and extended using a panel of persons working at the same plant in 2009 and 2010 (134 extra code combinations added)

sample.universe: Danish residents aged 30-60 at the beginning of the base year, present in the basic population registers in the base year and 1-5 years earlier and employed two years before the base year, for base years 2000-2005
sample.unit_of_observation: individual (one observation per person, with a single base year t and outcomes measured in t+4)
selection_rules: Persons who had their first cancer diagnosis as 29-61-year-olds in 2000-2005 according to the cancer register (any C diagnosis according to ICD10): 62,305
Exclusion of skin cancer cases (C43 and C44 diagnoses): 44,870

Exclusion of persons who, according to the hospitalisation register, had any diagnosis of cancer or benign tumour (C or D00-D49 diagnosis) in a year prior to the year of the first diagnosis in the cancer register: 36,547
Exclusion of persons who are not in the basic population registers in the year of diagnosis and 1-5 years before the diagnosis: 35,220
Exclusion of persons who are not 30-60 years of age at the beginning of the year of diagnosis: 33,617
Exclusion of persons who were not employed (most of the year) 2 years before the year of diagnosis: 25,094
Main analysis conditions on survival until the end of the fifth year after the year of diagnosis: 5750 male and 9282 female cancer survivors

Control group: all 30-60-year-olds not diagnosed with cancer or benign tumours in 2000-2005 or earlier, employed in year t-2 and in the registers in all years from t-5 to t; 10 x N drawn randomly by base year, gender and age without replacement across base years
sample.period: base years 2000-2005; outcomes in t+4 (2004-2009); covariates from t-5 to t-2
sample.n_observations: 120,072 males and 140,803 females in the main employment regressions (Table 4)
sample.n_individuals: 25,094 cancer cases after exclusions; 5750 male and 9282 female five-year survivors; control groups of 114,322 males and 131,521 females (Table 2)

construction_notes: Earnings, wages, income and disposable income are measured in DKK 1000 per year and the hourly wage rate in DKK, all adjusted to 2000 prices using the consumer price index (USD 1 is approximately DKK 6)

Employment: a person is categorised as unemployed if unemployed for half of the year or more, and as employed if not unemployed and earnings are the dominant source of income; for employees earnings must also exceed about DKK 45,000 (about USD 7500 in 2000 prices)

Outlier exclusion in the earnings and income regressions: observations with values of the dependent variable below zero or above 1000 (DKK 1 m / USD 167,000), and above DKK 1000 (USD 167) for the hourly wage rate

The six job characteristics variables are first principal components of sets of O*NET variables with loadings above 0.75, extracted from individual-level Danish data for 2010-12 weighted by the observed occupational frequency, and normalised to mean zero and standard deviation one in the Danish workforce

Cognitive skills = (Analytical skills + Interpersonal skills)/2 and Manual skills = (Physical strength + Fine motor skills)/2, defined to reduce collinearity (correlations of 0.93-0.94 between analytical and interpersonal skills and 0.86 between fine motor and physical strength for men)
In regressions where job characteristics in t-2 are explanatory variables, missing values are set to zero and a dummy for missing job characteristics is included

Job characteristics of non-unique (aggregated) DISCO codes are simple averages of the characteristics of the underlying unique codes; 594 unique DISCO88, 564 unique DISCO08 and 877 unique US SOC codes are observed

'Same occupation in t+4 as in t-2' is defined at the 4-digit DISCO level (377 values); 'same industry' uses Statistics Denmark's 111-grouping of industries; occupation codes and plant identifiers are missing in t-2 or t+4 for about 15% and 25% of those employed in t+4
Covariates are measured in t-2 and earlier but not in t-1, because individuals diagnosed in year t could already have been affected by symptoms in t-1

links.pointer_quote: For both genders, cancer reduces the probability of being employed in the fourth year after diagnosis by about 7 percentage points, relative to the non-cancer group.

heterogeneity.finding: an increase in cognitive skill requirements at t-2 by 1 standard deviation reduces the negative employment effect by about 2 percentage points for males (0.022, col (2)) and about 1 percentage point for females (0.013, col (6))

an increase in manual skill requirements by 1 standard deviation enhances the negative employment effect by 1.4 percentage points for females (-0.014, col (6)); no significant gradient for males (-0.002, col (2))

for males the effect is about -10 percentage points for the compulsory-schooling reference group and about -5 for the further education group (col (3)); the gradient is smaller for females (col (7)) and substantially smaller for both genders once interactions with job characteristics are included (cols (4) and (8))
breast cancer reduces the employment probability by 5.9 percentage points, other cancers by 7.8 percentage points (Table B3)
localised cancer reduces the employment probability by 5.5 (males) and 4.4 (females) percentage points; non-localised cancer by 9.3 and 8.5 percentage points (Tables B4 and B5)
excluding individuals aged 55-60 in the base year does not significantly affect the estimated effects (Table B2)
